Sequence confirmed and the brief's narrative (not checker 1's correction) is right: Ozimals the company closed in 2016; the validation server was then run by a volunteer, Malkavyn Eldritch; in May 2017 Edward Distelhurst / Akimeta Ltd (claiming Ozimals owed him money) sent a cease-and-desist demanding he stop using Ozimals IP; Eldritch shut the server ('I do not have the means to fight this in court'). Corrections: (a) not ALL bunnies hibernated: before shutdown Ozimals had given away items that make rabbits not need food (and leave them sterile), and Boing Boing says 'some rabbits will live on forever'; (b) 'permanent' is the BBC's word; mechanically rabbits hibernate after 72h unfed and wake if fed, so permanence follows from no server existing; (c) Ozimals Pufflings died instantly when servers went down.

~500,000 MAU (Oct 2024) confirmed: Voyager relays an interview with Linden Lab's owner giving roughly 500k MAU in mid/late Oct 2024; a community comment notes MAU is only released occasionally by LL. Region count: Voyager's Nov 2024 grid stats give 27,729 total (17,923 private estates, 9,806 Linden-owned), not 27,769; the 27,769 figure may be a different week's count but was not found. Concurrency: no source gives a '12-month average peak' of 49,649; Voyager's series are daily maxima: 2025 high 49,798 (24 Mar 2025); 2026 high 48,802 (1 Mar 2026); monthly maxima Jun-Sep 2026 of 44,931 / 43,822 / 45,483 / 43,891. Regions had fallen to 27,192 by mid-June 2026. Recommend quoting '~45-50k peak concurrency, ~27.2-27.7k regions'; the density arithmetic (1-2 people per region) still holds, and it is an upper bound because concurrency counts bots.

arXiv 2411.00114 'Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization' (Altera.AL) exists and its abstract covers 10-1000+ agents, PIANO (Parallel Information Aggregation via Neural Orchestration), Minecraft, specialized roles, adherence to and changing of collective rules, cultural and religious transmission; the authors call the findings 'preliminary'. MIT Technology Review (27 Nov 2024) confirms up to 1,000 agents, tax votes swayed by pro/anti-tax agents, Pastafarian seeding in a 500-agent run, and that runs lasted 12 in-game days (4 wall-clock hours). Corrections: cite the preprint rather than 'its own video'; the '32% of all Minecraft items' figure did not appear in any extract across two searches and should be flagged as unconfirmed (it may be in the paper body, which could not be fetched). 'Unverified company claims' remains fair: no independent replication found.

Pivot confirmed by Inworld's own blog ('The new AI infrastructure for scaling games, media, and characters') and docs: Runtime is 'Inworld's new AI orchestration platform' providing 'the same tools that powered AI characters in Studio as a composable toolkit'; the arcanumrpgs explainer reports a docs page stating 'the legacy Inworld Character Studio has been retired'. TTS at $5 per million characters confirmed for Inworld-TTS-1 (fish.audio comparison; TTS-1-Max $10/M). $500M valuation (Aug 2023 round) appears in TechCrunch/Lightspeed results. Caveats: the 'March to September 2025' window is only the third-party blog's framing; TTS-1/TTS-1-Max are now marked deprecated in Inworld's model docs in favour of TTS-1.5-mini/max (prices not confirmed), so the $5 figure is a 2025 price, not current; Runtime docs still mention 'Character Studio directly in-engine', so some in-engine character tooling survives under the Runtime name.

Announcement late Oct 2025 (Bloomberg/TechCrunch 29 Oct 2025): open-ended chats for under-18s to end by 25 Nov 2025; interim cap 'starts at two hours per day and goes down over the following weeks'; age assurance via in-house behavioural tool plus Persona; teens shifted to prompt-based story/visual creation. Settlement: court filings in early Jan 2026 (one outlet says 14 Jan) show Google and Character.AI agreed to settle the Florida (Garcia/Setzer) case plus Colorado, New York and Texas suits; terms undisclosed; M.D. Fla. dismissed the case with 90 days to finalize; Google's exposure stems from its $2.7B 2024 licensing deal and rehiring of the founders.

SAG-AFTRA announced on 19 May 2025 an NLRB unfair labor practice charge against Llama Productions LLC (Epic-owned) for launching the AI Vader 'without providing any notice of their intent to do this and without bargaining with us over appropriate terms'; James Earl Jones's family had approved the use. No reported outcome found as of this search (the charge copy carried no docket number); a ULP charge is an allegation investigated by the regional office, not a finding. Open question in the brief remains open.

Steam half confirmed: Totally Human Media (Ichiro Lambe) analysis as of 13 Jul 2025 found 7,818 of ~114,126 Steam games (~7%) with gen-AI disclosures and ~20% of 2025 releases; ~800% up on the ~1,000-title 2024 baseline (Apr 2024 study: 1.1%); ~60% of disclosed uses were visual assets; disclosures are a floor. Quantic Foundry half corrected: the 18 Dec 2025 post reports an optional survey of 1,799 respondents (Oct-Dec 2025) in which 85% were below neutral and 63% (62.7%) chose the most negative option; the '>1.75M gamers' figure in secondary write-ups is an error (it is the size of Quantic Foundry's cumulative profile dataset, not this survey's N). Segmentation: women/non-binary and younger and story-focused gamers more negative; older and power-progression-motivated gamers more favourable. TechRaptor separately found 18% of Steam's top 100 2025 releases used gen-AI.

additional_findings: Method: page fetching is blocked in this sandbox; all verdicts rest on search-result extracts (12 searches, standard mode except one extended). No primary page was read in full.

Ozimals end-of-life detail: before the server shutdown Ozimals had distributed items that make rabbits food-independent but sterile, and those rabbits survived; Pufflings (a second Ozimals breedable) died instantly. Design lesson: a 'perma-pet' escape hatch that trades reproduction for independence from life-support servers is a proven end-of-life mechanism and should be built in from day one, not improvised. The 2017 claimant was Edward Distelhurst / Akimeta Ltd, a creditor asserting IP ownership, so creditor claims on a dead vendor's IP are a distinct failure mode from DMCA fights between vendors.

Second Life 2026 trajectory (Daniel Voyager series): daily-maximum concurrency 49,798 (24 Mar 2025) -> 48,802 (1 Mar 2026) -> ~43.8-45.5k monthly maxima Jun-Sep 2026; regions 27,729 (Nov 2024) -> 27,192 (Jun 2026, about -2%). Density is still falling slowly; the brief's 1-2 people per region is an upper bound because concurrency counts bots. A summary of a Dec 2024 VentureBeat interview attributes ~$650M annual revenue to Linden Lab's owner (unverified); Linden's CEO cited 900k MAU in the mid-2010s, so 500k is roughly a 45% decline.

Quantic Foundry segmentation matters for audience targeting: hostility to gen-AI is strongest among women/non-binary, younger and story-motivated players, weakest among older and power-progression-motivated players. A successor world aimed at social/story players faces the most hostile segment and needs the strongest disclosure posture.

Project Sid runs lasted 4 wall-clock hours (12 in-game days) and the authors call the findings preliminary; it is evidence about short-horizon emergence, not persistent worlds. A 2026 arXiv literature on long-horizon agent societies now exists that the brief does not cover: Agentopia (2606.07513), OpenLife (2606.31046), Emergence World (2606.08367), Interaction Theater (2602.20059), Superminds Test (2604.22452) and a Moltbook socialization case study (2602.14299). Worth a follow-up pass for the taxonomy.

Inworld's TTS-1 ($5/M chars) and TTS-1-Max ($10/M) are already deprecated in favour of TTS-1.5-mini/max (pricing unconfirmed); vendor pricing in this space turns over within a year, so cost-per-NPC-hour models should be parameterised, not hard-coded. Inworld's WishRoll testimonial ('one million users in 19 days with over 20x cost reduction') is vendor-published.

Character.AI's minors policy replaces open chat with prompt-based collaborative story/visual creation and uses behavioural age inference plus Persona; the Setzer settlement needs court approval within 90 days of early Jan 2026 and terms are sealed, so no liability precedent is set. Google's $2.7B licensing deal is what pulled it into the suits: licensing a companion-AI model carries litigation exposure.
The SAG-AFTRA Fortnite Vader NLRB charge had no reported disposition in search results; the next step is the NLRB public case search for Llama Productions LLC (May 2025).

Steam disclosure: ~60% of disclosed uses are visual-asset generation; VGC reports Valve has since 'significantly' rewritten its AI disclosure rules (date not captured), so any Steam-distribution plan for a live-LLM world should re-read the current rules.
